text_rules: Keep cover text to 3-5 punchy words mixing Hindi+English with at least one number (₹ amount, GSM, piece count, or a loss figure); frame it as a question or disaster outcome to create an open curiosity loop — never answer the question on the thumbnail itself.
layout: Place all text in the vertical 25%-70% safe zone (center of the 9:16 frame), using large bold sans-serif type with thick black stroke; product or fabric close-up fills the background — skip face shots, let the yellow-highlighted keyword be the single visual anchor.
patterns: Top-performing Indian business Reels thumbnails follow a 'money-at-risk + specific number' formula — a rupee loss figure or piece count paired with a failure keyword (Crack, Reject, Scam, Wasted) instantly signals stakes. Yellow (#FFD400) keyword highlight against white body text on a dark or product-hero background dominates the highest-view covers; cream/pastel or illustration-based covers with no numbers consistently flatline. Hinglish (Hindi question + English technical term like GSM, DTF, YARN) outperforms pure Hindi or pure English because it matches how Indian B2B buyers actually talk.
ig_patterns: High-save Reels covers promise a reusable checklist or diagnostic ('Check These 3 Things', '3 Checks That Save') — the thumbnail implies lasting reference value the viewer will need again, driving bookmarks. High-share covers frame a specific disaster with a relatable ₹ loss amount (₹40K, ₹50K, ₹25K) that triggers 'my retailer friend is making this exact mistake' forwarding impulse. Both save and share leaders use the proven formula: ₹-amount or piece-count + technical keyword in yellow + failure/question hook in white — zero illustration, zero cream/pastel, zero pure-Hindi educational framing.
